## Purpose and Scope

This RAD provides illustrative patterns for realizing the Software Supply Chain Security capability. It is the primary consumption point for:

- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23 — Software Bill of Materials](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23.md)
- [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24 — Dependency Integrity Verification](../abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24.md)
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#rad-scope]

### RAD Scope

- SBOM generation at build time and its integration with artifact signing
- Dependency integrity verification at install and build stages
- SBOM-based vulnerability correlation and continuous monitoring
- Integration with the SCA capability and the image scanning capability

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#capability-domain-boundary]

### Capability Domain Boundary

Software Supply Chain Security covers the integrity and provenance of all software components consumed by enterprise applications, from initial dependency fetch through production artifact deployment. It does not cover runtime vulnerability exploitation (Application Security Testing / WAF) or endpoint security for developer workstations.

| SBOM generation infrastructure | **Owns** | Advises | — |
| Dependency lock file enforcement | Supports | Advises | **Owns** |
| SBOM-based vulnerability correlation | **Owns** | Advises | Informs |

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Dependency Install / Build] -->|Lock File / Hash Check| B[Dependency Integrity Verification]
    B -->|Integrity Fail| C[Block Build + Alert]
    B -->|Pass| D[Application Build]

    F --> G[Vulnerability Correlation Service]
    G -->|New CVE Match| H[Alert to Development Team]
    D --> I[Artifact Signing]
    E -->|Signed SBOM Attestation| I

    J --> K[Admission Control]
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#logical-components]

### Logical Components

| Component | Type | Architectural Role |
|---|---|---|
| Dependency Integrity Verifier | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DEPINT-2.7.24 | Hash and lock file verification at install/build time |
| SBOM Generator | ABB Realization — GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SBOM-2.7.23 | Produces SBOM from completed build artifact |
| SBOM Store | Logical Repository | Stores SBOM documents associated with artifact versions |
| Vulnerability Correlation Service | Integration | Cross-references SBOM against CVE feeds continuously |
| Artifact Signing Service | Logical Component | Signs build artifacts and SBOM attestations |
| Admission Controller | Pipeline / Runtime | Verifies artifact signatures before promotion or deployment |

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#pattern-1-build-time-sbom-generation-with-attestation]

### Pattern 1: Build-Time SBOM Generation with Attestation

**When to use**: All application builds that produce a deployable artifact.

**Logical flow**:
1. Build completes successfully
2. SBOM generator produces a machine-readable inventory of all components in the artifact
3. SBOM document is signed and stored alongside the artifact in the artifact registry
4. Artifact and its SBOM attestation are available for downstream verification and audit
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#pattern-2-dependency-integrity-gate-at-install]

### Pattern 2: Dependency Integrity Gate at Install

**When to use**: All builds that install third-party dependencies.

**Logical flow**:
1. Dependency installation step uses lock files to specify exact versions and expected hashes
2. Integrity verifier checks downloaded packages against expected hashes
3. Any mismatch is treated as an integrity failure; the build is aborted and an alert is generated
4. No dependency is installed without a corresponding lock file entry
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#pattern-3-continuous-sbom-based-vulnerability-monitoring]

### Pattern 3: Continuous SBOM-Based Vulnerability Monitoring

**When to use**: All production artifacts with a stored SBOM.

**Logical flow**:
1. Vulnerability feed update arrives (new CVE published)
2. Correlation service cross-references the CVE against all stored SBOMs
3. Affected artifact versions are identified and development teams are notified
4. Development teams assess impact and prioritize remediation based on production exposure

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#deployment-context-considerations]

## Deployment Context Considerations

| Context | Architectural Consideration |
|---|---|
| Cloud-native (container-based) | Container image SBOM can be embedded as an OCI artifact annotation; image signing integrates naturally with container registry |
| Multi-language monorepo | SBOM generation must cover all language ecosystems present in the build; a unified SBOM aggregator may be needed |
| Regulated environment | SBOM retention and auditability requirements may specify minimum retention periods and access controls on SBOM storage |

page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-APP-RA-SUPPLY-CHAIN-2.7.31.md#constraints-and-exceptions]

## Constraints and Exceptions

- Lock file enforcement may conflict with dependency resolution patterns used by some languages; migration to lock-file-based workflows must be planned.
- SBOM format standardization (SPDX vs. CycloneDX) should be defined at the enterprise level to enable consistent tooling across teams.
- Continuous vulnerability monitoring requires that SBOM storage is maintained and updated when artifacts are patched or replaced; stale SBOM data reduces monitoring fidelity.
